title: A form seen only through devotion

verses.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचमया प्रसन्नेन तवार्जुनेदंरूपं परं दर्शितमात्मयोगात् । तेजोमयं विश्वमनन्तमाद्यंयन्मे त्वदन्येन न दृष्टपूर्वम् ॥
verses.tr: Krishna says: O Arjuna, I have shown you this supreme, radiant, endless, original form through my grace. No one except you has seen it before.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Arjuna has just asked to see Krishna’s familiar form again after the overwhelming cosmic vision. Krishna answers that the vision itself came by his grace and power, and that Arjuna has been given a sight no one else has received.

body.text: Krishna says: O Arjuna, I have shown you this supreme, radiant, endless, original form through my grace. No one except you has seen it before. Krishna says he has shown this form to Arjuna through his own power and grace, and that no one else has ever seen it before. Krishna says this form cannot be seen by any ritual act in the human world, except by Arjuna.

verses.sa: न वेदयज्ञाध्ययनैर्न दानैर्न च क्रियाभिर्न तपोभिरुग्रैः । एवंरूपः शक्य अहं नृलोकेद्रष्टुं त्वदन्येन कुरुप्रवीर ॥
verses.tr: I cannot be seen in this form in the human world by study of the Vedas, sacrifice, charity, severe austerity, or ritual acts, except by you, Arjuna.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna continues, naming every path to the divine and saying they fall short of this vision. Listen to the one exception.

body.text: I cannot be seen in this form in the human world by study of the Vedas, sacrifice, charity, severe austerity, or ritual acts, except by you, Arjuna. Krishna lists study of the Vedas, sacrifice, charity, severe austerity, and ritual acts, then says this form is not seen by any of them except by you, Arjuna. Krishna then asks Arjuna to set aside his fear and look once more at his familiar form.

verses.sa: मा ते व्यथा मा च विमूढभावोदृष्ट्वा रूपं घोरमीदृङ्ममेदम् । व्यपेतभीः प्रीतमनाः पुनस्त्वंतदेव मे रूपमिदं प्रपश्य ॥
verses.tr: Do not be distressed or confused by this fierce form of mine. Free from fear and calm-minded, look again upon this very form of mine.
verses.angle: Krishna asks Arjuna to drop fear and confusion
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: After the cosmic vision, Arjuna is shaken. Krishna now asks him to let go of fear and confusion.

body.text: Do not be distressed or confused by this fierce form of mine. Free from fear and calm-minded, look again upon this very form of mine. Krishna tells Arjuna to drop distress and confusion, and to look again with a calm, pleased mind. Sanjaya describes Krishna returning to his gentle form, reassuring the frightened Arjuna.

verses.sa: सञ्जय उवाचइत्यर्जुनं वासुदेवस्तथोक्त्वास्वकं रूपं दर्शयामास भूयः । आश्वासयामास च भीतमेनंभूत्वा पुनः सौम्यवपुर्महात्मा ॥
verses.tr: Sanjaya says: After speaking thus to Arjuna, Vasudeva revealed his own form again. The great one then reassured the frightened Arjuna, taking once more a gentle form.
verses.angle: sauyamya-vapuh: the gentle form that ends fear
verses.speaker: Sanjaya

intro.text: Arjuna has just seen the terrifying cosmic form and trembles. Listen to how Krishna answers his fear.

body.text: Sanjaya says: After speaking thus to Arjuna, Vasudeva revealed his own form again. The great one then reassured the frightened Arjuna, taking once more a gentle form. Krishna, the great one, returns to a gentle form, saumya-vapuh, and reassures the frightened Arjuna. The terror ends not with a command, but with mercy. Arjuna tells Krishna that seeing this gentle form has restored his calm and his natural state.

verses.sa: अर्जुन उवाचदृष्ट्वेदं मानुषं रूपं तवसौम्यं जनार्दन । इदानीमस्मि संवृत्तः सचेताः प्रकृतिं गतः ॥
verses.tr: Arjuna says: Seeing your gentle human form, Janardana, I am calm again and restored to my natural state.
verses.angle: Samyavrittah, restored, back to his own nature
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: After the cosmic terror, Krishna returns to his gentle human form. Listen for the word that shows Arjuna is back to himself.

body.text: Arjuna says: Seeing your gentle human form, Janardana, I am calm again and restored to my natural state. Listen to the word samyavrittah, restored. After the cosmic terror, Arjuna says he is restored and returned to his natural state. Krishna says the gentle form is easy, but the cosmic one is hard to behold, and even the radiant beings long for it.

verses.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचसुदुर्दर्शमिदं रूपं दृष्टवानसि यन्मम । देवा अप्यस्य रूपस्य नित्यं दर्शनकाङ्क्षिणः ॥
verses.tr: Krishna says: The form you have seen is very hard to behold. Even the radiant beings long forever to see it.
verses.angle: Radiant beings always long to see this form
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Arjuna has just been steadied by Krishna's human form after being overwhelmed by the cosmic vision. Now Krishna explains what Arjuna has just been allowed to see.

body.text: Krishna says: The form you have seen is very hard to behold. Even the radiant beings long forever to see it. The most telling thing is that even the radiant beings always long to see this form. The vision Arjuna has just been given is rarer than anything even the divine beings can behold. Krishna then says that this form cannot be seen through the Vedas, austerity, charity, or sacrifice.

verses.sa: नाहं वेदैर्न तपसा न दानेन न चेज्यया । शक्य एवंविधो द्रष्टुं दृष्टवानसि मां यथा ॥
verses.tr: I cannot be seen in this form through the Vedas, austerity, charity, or sacrifice, as you have seen me.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna now turns to what cannot be done. Listen for the four paths he sets aside.

body.text: I cannot be seen in this form through the Vedas, austerity, charity, or sacrifice, as you have seen me. Krishna lists four standard ways to the divine, Vedas, austerity, charity, and sacrifice, and says none of them can produce the sight Arjuna has just had. He then tells Arjuna that only undivided devotion can truly reveal him.

verses.sa: भक्त्या त्वनन्यया शक्यमहमेवंविधोऽर्जुन । ज्ञातुं दृष्टुं च तत्त्वेन प्रवेष्टुं च परंतप ॥
verses.tr: But only through undivided devotion can I be truly known, seen, and entered, Arjuna.
verses.angle: Ananyaya: undivided devotion is the key
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: After showing his cosmic form, Krishna now names the one path that can reach him. Listen for the exact word he uses.

body.text: But only through undivided devotion can I be truly known, seen, and entered, Arjuna. Krishna says that knowing, seeing, and entering him is possible, shakya, but only through ananyaya, undivided devotion. Ordinary effort and ritual cannot do this. Krishna now lists the qualities of the devotee who comes to him, free from attachment and enmity.

verses.sa: मत्कर्मकृन्मत्परमो मद्भक्तः सङ्गवर्जितः । निर्वैरः सर्वभूतेषु यः स मामेति पाण्डव ॥
verses.tr: O Pandava, the devotee who works for Me alone, takes Me as the highest goal, is devoted to Me, is free from attachment, and bears no enmity toward any being, comes to Me.
verses.angle: sarvabhuteshu: no enmity toward any being
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna finishes the description of the true devotee by naming four qualities that must be present together. Listen to how they fit.

body.text: O Pandava, the devotee who works for Me alone, takes Me as the highest goal, is devoted to Me, is free from attachment, and bears no enmity toward any being, comes to Me. The word sarvabhuteshu means toward all beings, and it closes the door on any hostility. The devotee must bear no enmity toward any being, and that is the price of reaching Me. Arjuna now asks a practical question about which of these two paths is better for most people.
